{{Short description|Theorem for nilmanifolds}}
In [[differential geometry]], '''Mal'cev's criterion''', proved by [[Anatoly Maltsev|Anatoly Mal'cev]], states that a [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] [[Nilpotent Lie algebra|nilpotent]] [[Lie group]] admits a lattice, i.e., a [[Discrete space|discrete]] [[Cocompact group action|co-compact]] [[subgroup]], if and only if the [[Lie group–Lie algebra correspondence|associated]] [[Lie algebra]] admits a basis such that the [[structure constants]] are rational.{{sfn|Eberlein|2003|p=38}}

The relevance of Mal'cev's criterion comes from the fact that it gives us a one-to-one correspondence between isomorphism classes of Lie algebras with rational structure constants and [[Compact space|compact]] [[Nilmanifold|nilmanifolds]]. Indeed, Mal'cev showed that compact nilmanifolds are precisely quotients of simply connected nilpotent Lie groups by a lattice.{{sfn|Eberlein|2004|p=69}}

== Relevance in Kähler geometry ==
Mal'cev's criterion is relevant in [[Kähler manifold|Kähler geometry]] because compact nilmanifolds with a Kähler structure must be [[diffeomorphism|diffeomorphic]] to a [[torus]].{{sfn|Benson|Gordon|1988}}{{sfn|Hasegawa|1989}} Therefore, when looking for manifolds that do not admit a Kähler structure, one may use Mal'cev's criterion to generate a compact nilmanifold from any rational Lie algebra.{{sfn|Hasegawa|1989}}
By constructing other structures on the manifold, such as a [[Complex manifold|complex]] or [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic]] structure, one finds a non-Kähler manifold of said structure. It therefore helps finding solutions to the [[Thurston–Weinstein problem]], which concerns itself with the existence of non-Kähler symplectic manifolds.{{sfn|Benson|Gordon|1988}}
